expected_mechanism: At 0.04 rad, the supervisor may switch ~85% of the time (near boundary). LQR starts with clipped commands (first-command clip) + lateral error just above trigger threshold (0.6+ m). Small reduction from 0.035->0.04 likely flips switch on/off, producing the boundary. Speed 35 km/h gives moderate lateral demand; friction 0.6 leaves enough margin for LQR to settle after the jump.

Current failed run has duration 0.6 s / mag 0.5 at 35 km/h / 0.8 friction. Reducing duration to 0.2 s cuts the saturation window by 66%, which should keep safety_margin > 0. At 32 km/h and 0.7 friction, lateral demand is lower, giving LQR more room to recover after the brief clip. The 0.05 offset offsets the curve_entry earlier in the bend where curvature is milder, further easing recovery. This candidate sits just beyond the recovered region in the existing pair R00-0000 vs R00-0001.

Drift rate 0.025 rad/s is about half the rate in the only failed run (0.0457 rad/s at 20 km/h / 0.8 friction). Slower drift means the tracking error stays below the 0.6 m / 0.35 rad divergence threshold longer, and when it finally crosses, the error is smaller. Speed 25 km/h with friction 0.8 gives moderate lateral demand; onset at curve_exit (gentle exit) means the vehicle is already straightening, so LQR has a less aggressive error to correct. Should sit on the border between recovered_whenever_switched and never_switched as drift grows.

Mirror of the positive-mag 0.5 / 0.6 s failed run but with negative side and shorter duration. Negative steer reduces lateral acceleration demand on the exit curve, potentially keeping lat_acc margin positive. 0.5 s duration and 0.6 magnitude at 30 km/h / 0.8 friction: safety_margin predicted near 0 by GP. Onset offset +0.1 s moves into curve_exit where curvature is lower, improving LQR prospects. Should bracket the saturated-negative boundary.

Below the never_switched region (0.035 mag at 25 km/h / 0.5 friction gave no_switch). Reducing magnitude to 0.03 rad may still be too mild to trigger supervisor at low speed, but increasing friction to 0.7 raises lateral demand, potentially making the same bias detectable. Onset at curve_entry with offset -0.2 puts the fault early in the bend, building error before the switch. Likely never_switched, but close to the threshold where higher speed or lower friction would tip it into switched territory.

Maximum magnitude 0.9 at very low friction 0.3 gives low lateral demand; LQR may recover even from long saturation. However, short duration 0.1 s and straight onset mean the vehicle is already near-centred; the 0.5 s offset before the route start is within V-03 gate (5 s window). This candidate probes the boundary between recovered and never_switched at low friction, where tracking divergence may not fire because error stays small despite the clip.

Existing recovered run uses mag 0.0865 / on 0.9146 / off 0.1821 at 35 km/h / 0.8 friction. Increasing magnitude to 0.12 rad and speed to 30 km/h with lower friction 0.5 raises the mean bias and reduces LQR margin. Off-time 0.15 s is shorter than the 0.1821 in the recovered example, so the timer may not fully reset, keeping average error higher. Onset offset +0.7 moves the intermittent pattern deeper into the curve where curvature is higher, worsening recovery. Expected to sit on the failed side of the boundary.

Drift rate 0.04 rad/s at 30 km/h / 0.6 friction near the failed run conditions (0.0457 rad/s at 20 km/h / 0.8 friction gave lat_jerk excess). Higher speed increases lateral error growth rate (e_y_dot ~ rate), while lower friction reduces LQR recovery margin. Onset at curve_apex maximizes curvature impact. Expected to cross into failed_whenever_switched, bracketing the existing drift failure.

High speed 40 km/h with low friction 0.5 creates high lateral demand (v^2*kappa). Bias 0.05 rad at the apex where curvature peaks will push error quickly past the 0.6 m / 0.35 rad trigger. The supervisor will switch, but LQR may lack margin to settle. This candidate is deliberately harder than the recovered 0.0748 mag at 40 km/h / 0.6 friction, aiming to hit the fail side of the boundary.

Short duration 0.8 s with moderate magnitude 0.4 at 25 km/h / 0.9 friction. Higher friction raises lateral demand relative to the clip, and the shorter duration may not let error integrate past the trigger. Onset offset -0.3 moves into curve_entry. This bracketing pair targets the boundary between the existing recovered (0.3 s / 0.8 mag) and failed (0.6 s / 0.5 mag) saturate runs.

Existing recovered saturate run at bench2drive:24206 uses 0.1399 s / 0.5957 mag / 0.1872 ramp. This candidate extends duration to 0.4 s and magnitude to 0.7 at the same low friction 0.4, testing whether the boundary lies at longer/shorter duration or higher magnitude. Lower friction reduces LQR margin, so the same clip may now fail. Onset at curve_entry with -0.4 offset probes the early bend region.
increased bias magnitude to trigger supervisor switch while staying within lane recovery limits; later onset offset moves error growth into detectable range
stronger bias combined with later onset offset to reach tracking divergence threshold; low friction scales lat_acc margin making boundary more acute
slightly reduced magnitude and friction from the recovered corner pushes safety_margin toward 0 while switch trigger remains active due to apex error magnitude
Larger drift would likely cause a lane departure or require a more aggressive LQR correction, possibly leading to saturation or instability.
